title: Home filmed without my consent: CJP spokesperson Saurav Das
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) alleged that certain YouTubers and media persons had entered his residence and filmed inside without consent, calling it “a serious invasion of privacy” and a security threat to him and his family. He is in Maharashtra to attend a two-day meeting of Citizens for Justice and Peace.

In a post on X, Mr. Das claimed that around 15 to 20 people had gathered outside his residence on Wednesday (August 5) morning, with some camping there since the previous night.

“It’s not just an invasion of my privacy but also a grave security threat to me and my family,” Mr. Das wrote. He said that if “anti-social elements” attacked him at his residence because of the videos, the YouTubers and those allegedly coordinating them would be directly responsible.

‘Police deployed’

An officer from the South district police told The Hindu that security personnel had been deployed outside Mr. Das’s residence after he raised the issue on X.

The officer said that since Mr. Das was not in Delhi, he had authorised someone to submit a draft complaint at the Greater Kailash police station on his behalf. “The complaint would be formally lodged, following which an investigation would be carried out,” the officer added.

Mr. Das’s post drew political reactions, with Aam Aadmi Party national convener and former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal saying that “this is the real face of Modi”.

Trinamool Congress MP Derek O’Brien said the matter had been raised by his party in the Rajya Sabha onWednesday (August 5) afternoon.

title: Permission for Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event in Prayagraj revoked by venue provider
author: PTI
content_html:
The Kayastha Pathshala Trust has revoked permission for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme, scheduled to be held at K.P. Ground in Prayagraj on August 8, citing an Allahabad High Court order.

The trust also cited waterlogging at the venue for the cancellation.

The trust's acting president, Jitendra Nath Chaudhary, told PTI that the Allahabad High Court, in an order dated August 14, 2025, had directed that the KP College ground should not be used for purposes other than sports and educational activities.

He said the ground was also waterlogged after rain and was unsafe for a public event. Mr. Chaudhary said the permission granted to the Congress was conditional upon approval from the district magistrate.

The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha was scheduled to interact with students on alleged paper leaks and other matters affecting students at the gathering.

Appeal to government

On Wednesday, Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai visited Prayagraj to review preparations for the event.

Mr. Rai asserted that Mr. Gandhi will come to Prayagraj on August 8 and interact with students despite the KP Trust revoking permission for the venue.

Addressing reporters in the evening, Mr. Rai urged the state government and district administration to provide an alternative venue for the programme.

He alleged that the BJP government was "afraid" of Mr. Gandhi and claimed the event was being obstructed for political reasons.

Mr. Gandhi's programmes in Kota and Dehradun had similarly been cancelled, Mr. Rai claimed.

title: KSRTC to launch inter-State Flybus service from Bengaluru airport to Kozhikode from August 15
author: Darshan Devaiah B.P.
content_html:
The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) will launch an inter-State Flybus service connecting Kempegowda International Airport (KIA), Bengaluru, with Kozhikode in Kerala from August 15.

The new premium airport bus service has been introduced to provide seamless connectivity for air passengers travelling between Bengaluru airport and north Kerala, while also benefiting passengers from Mysuru and parts of Kodagu, according to officials.

The KSRTC Flybus is a premium, non-stop Volvo multi-axle airport coach service that connects KIA with major cities across Karnataka, including Mysuru, Madikeri, Kundapur, and Davangere. Designed to offer a comfortable, flight-like travel experience, the service also provides passengers with complimentary snack kits containing water, beverages and local snacks.

Timings

According to KSRTC, the Flybus will depart from KIA at 10.45 p.m. every day and reach Kozhikode at 7.15 a.m. the following morning. The return service will leave Kozhikode at 7.30 p.m. and arrive at Bengaluru airport at 4.15 a.m.

En route, the service will operate via Yelahanka, Hebbal, Nayandahalli Metro Station, Mysuru, Hunsur, Gonikoppa, Ponnampet, Kutta, Mananthavadi, and Kalpetta, providing direct airport connectivity to passengers travelling from these regions.

The ticket fare from Kempegowda International Airport to Kozhikode has been fixed at ₹1,500 per passenger. Intermediate fares have also been announced, with Mysuru priced at ₹960, Gonikoppa at ₹1,200, Mananthavadi at ₹1,350, and Kalpetta at ₹1,400.

A source in KSRTC said that the new service marks an important milestone for the corporation’s airport connectivity network. “The service has been planned to offer a convenient and reliable travel option for air passengers from Kerala as well as Kodagu and Mysuru regions, eliminating the need for multiple transfers. We expect good patronage from both airport users and intercity passengers,” sources said.

Earlier inter state routes

The KSRTC Flybus service was first introduced in 2013 with a single multi-axle Volvo bus operating between KIA and Mysuru. What began as a pilot initiative soon gained popularity among travellers in Karnataka because of its convenience, comfort, and direct airport connectivity.

In 2018, KSRTC launched two inter-State Flybus services to Salem in Tamil Nadu and Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh. However, both services were later discontinued due to various reasons. With the launch of the Bengaluru Airport-Kozhikode service, KSRTC is once again entering the inter-State airport bus segment after several years, according to sources.

title: Bengaluru: Treated water sales up, but not yet at summer levels
author: K. V. Aditya Bharadwaj
content_html:
Amid a deficient monsoon this year due to the El Niño effect, the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) on July 5 banned the use of potable water for non-drinking purposes and mandated the use of treated water instead. Though the sale of treated water has increased sharply since then, it is yet to reach the summer levels seen earlier this year, indicating slow implementation of the BWSSB’s norms on the ground.

The sale of treated water rose by 80%, from 31.68 lakh litres in June to 57.32 lakh litres in July. However, this remained 42% lower than the 1.05 crore litres sold through tankers in April this year. 

“The sale of treated water has increased significantly compared to previous months, and we expect it to rise further. We are also booking those who violate our water usage regulations,” said N. Manjula, chairperson, BWSSB. From July 5 till the end of the month, BWSSB booked nearly 800 cases for violations of water usage norms and levied penalties of around ₹30 lakh, several times higher than the revenue earned from the sale of treated water. The board sells treated water at a nominal cost of ₹10 per kilolitre and earned ₹2.23 lakh from its sale in July.

Construction sector

One of the biggest consumers of treated water in the city is the construction sector. Bhaskar T. Nagendrappa, president of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI) - Karnataka, said most large construction projects had already adopted the use of treated water. He urged the board to create greater public awareness about treated water so that homebuyers do not object to its use. He added that CREDAI had also appealed to the government to include the use of treated water and benchmark its parameters in the National Building Code of India, which guides construction activities.

Meanwhile, Amar Mysore, chairman of CREDAI-Bengaluru, said many large construction projects had set up treatment plants at project sites to further treat the water supplied by BWSSB and improve its quality.

However, smaller construction projects are yet to adopt the use of treated water, and many of them continue to rely on borewells dug on-site instead, industry insiders said.

Swimming pools 

BWSSB has mandated the use of treated water even for filling swimming pools, except those used by competitive athletes for training. However, most apartment communities are not willing to do this. “As it is, swimming pools are used by a small fraction of residents in any apartment community. People are not open to filling them with treated water. So, we have asked communities to stop topping up. We will not refill the pools with potable water, allowing them to dry out gradually,” said Satish Mallya, president, Bangalore Apartments’ Federation (BAF). He further said that apartments with swimming pools pay 25% extra in their water bills and appealed for a waiver when pools are not being filled with water supplied by the board.

Mapping apartment STPs to users

BWSSB is also working to promote the use of treated water produced at Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) at apartment complexes. At a recent meeting with BAF, Ms. Manjula directed board officials to draw up an action plan to map proximate users, such as construction projects and industries, with surplus treated water from apartment STPs. The board had earlier proposed drawing pipelines to supply treated water from apartment STPs to proximate users, but the plan yet to take off.

title: ‘Nambikkai Illam’ to be set up along Girivalam path in Tiruvannamalai
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
‘Nambikkai Illam’, a centre for persons with intellectual disabilities, will be coming up on the Girivalam path near Arunachaleswarar temple in Tiruvannamalai town as revenue officials have identified land for the new facility.

Along with health and revenue officials, Collector Vandana Garg and District Revenue Officer (DRO) A. Siva Subramanian has identified land near Government Arts and Science College along the path in the town.

The ‘Nambikkai Illam’ initiative was announced by State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson during the presentation of the Annual Budget for 2026-27 on Wednesday. “The new government facility will be a model one stop centre where all facilities and training for persons with intellectual disabilities will be provided. The identified land is located along a bus route and can be accessed easily,” M. Saradha, District Disabled Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu.

Officials of Welfare of Differently Abled Persons Department, which will maintain the facility, said that the new centre will provide special education, early intervention services, including physiotherapy, rehabilitation, and vocational training for children aged three and above. “The new government centre in Tiruvannamalai town will be the largest facility in terms of space with modern facilities,” Ms. Saradha said.

Officials said initially, the new facility would function as a day school between 9. 45 a.m and 5 p.m on all days, except Sundays. On an average, around 50 students would be enrolled at the centre which would have 13 staff led by the chief coordinator. Around 20 cents of government land have been identified for the purpose with a budgetary allocation of ₹4 crore.

At present, persons with intellectual disabilities, including children are taken care of in government-aided homes in the district. Officials had undertaken door-to-door visits to identify persons with intellectual disabilities and around 53,000 persons with disabilities have been identified in the district.

Officials also said that other Panchayat Unions such as Arani, Chengam, Kilpennathur, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Polur, Jamunamarathur, and Chetpet would have small centres for persons with intellectual disabilities in the coming months. These small centres would mostly operate at government hospitals in the area. Under ‘Nambikkai Illam’ initiative, similar centres would be set up in Thanjavur, Salem, Cuddalore, and Virudhunagar districts.
